newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Prosecutor halts Taiwan refinery repairs - monopoly.
newsitem.headline: Prosecutor halts Taiwan refinery repairs - monopoly.

text.p: Taiwan state monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp said on Tuesday a local prosecutor had halted repair work on its damaged Taoyuan refining unit until the cause of a May 29 explosion and fire is found.

Officials at the company's Taipei headquarters said the Taoyuan county district attorney's inquiry meant that Chinese Petroleum was unable to set a timetable for repairing the damaged unit, not to mention restarting it.
"Everything depends on the work of the district attorney," a company executive told Reuters by telephone.
In the meantime, he said, Chinese Petroleum would switch to imports of low-sulphur sweet crude so as to be able to continue producing jet fuel at the refinery.
The affected unit is the smaller of the plant's two hydro-desulfurising processors and has a daily capacity of 15,000 barrels. A 30,000-barrel unit is still in operation.
The official declined to say when such sweet crude shipments would begin or how much would be ordered.

On May 29, the day the hydro-desulfurising unit was to have been restarted after routine maintenance, an unexplained fire triggered a series of hydrogen explosions that damaged the unit and injured one worker.
The unit had been closed for annual maintenance since April 22 and had finished its scheduled checks on May 22 with no problems reported, officials said.
Company executives said on Tuesday that after nearly two weeks of investigation, officials still were trying to determine the cause of the initial fire.
Under Taiwan law, county prosecutors must be involved in such a disaster inquiry until it can be ascertained that no criminal acts were involved, executives said.
It was not known how long it would take before such a ruling could be reached in the Taoyuan inquiry.
The Taoyuan refinery mainly makes jet fuel, turning out 60,000 tonnes a month at full capacity. It is the principal supplier to Taipei's busy international airport at Taoyuan.
